execution_lifecycle_contract.admission: QueryExecutionFence owns one RLock, exact active leases and max_in_flight 1..32 default 8. UIR supplies one immutable epoch seed; acquire validates it and the normalized request, constructs the epoch and pin, reserves capacity and registers before any worker/provider call. Missing/ineligible/full/closed fails content-free before side effects.
execution_lifecycle_contract.deadline_and_join: Mint one absolute monotonic deadline. Provider deadline is min(total remaining, per-provider timeout). Interrupt acknowledgement and terminal join share one exact 1000 ms monotonic cleanup deadline after cancellation; accepted handles must guarantee terminal join inside it and are rejected before start otherwise. Interrupt once; no public return while nonterminal.
execution_lifecycle_contract.epoch_rotation: UIR submits one replacement seed; planner atomically replaces generation_ref, scope_ref and policy_digest under the fence lock and marks old leases cancelled there. No callback runs locked; supervisors interrupt/join outside. Old pins never become current again.

errors.timeout: provider_timeout only after ack and join

execution_lifecycle_contract.late_suppression: Worker writes only private handle state. Supervisor accepts only after joined, exact pin equality, uncancelled token, deadline and current-epoch recheck; fusion/outcome counters see no late value.
execution_lifecycle_contract.lexical_sqlite: Lexical adapter starts one non-daemon handle and calls search(query, execution=token). Retriever checkpoints before and after each snapshot read, before FTS, once per converted hit and before return. SQLite rejects expired work before connect, caps busy_timeout to max(1,min(configured,remaining_ms)), registers connection.interrupt before execute, installs a progress callback every 1000 VM opcodes, rechecks after row decode and clears the handler/interrupt registration and closes in finally.
execution_lifecycle_contract.ownership: UIR owns authoritative RuntimeGeneration, eligible SelectedScope and policy-digest seed values and requests replacement. Planner/fence alone constructs epochs, mints pins/leases, admits, cancels, publishes and releases. Providers/lexical/SQLite consume but cannot mint, rotate, extend or release.
execution_lifecycle_contract.provider_handle: Exact ProviderExecutionHandle carries the pin and lock-protected NEW->RUNNING->INTERRUPT_REQUESTED->TERMINAL->JOINED or RUNNING->TERMINAL->JOINED state, with one interrupt acknowledgement and terminal/joined readback. Planner admits no legacy query-only provider; each handle owns all provider thread/process resources.
execution_lifecycle_contract.release: One planner finally path removes the exact lease only after all handles are terminal/joined and callbacks cleared. release/cancel/interrupt/join are idempotent; foreign/duplicate lease identity fails closed.
